Here’s a quick, flavorful way to make an **Indian‑style steak** at home. The idea is to use classic Indian spices and a simple “tandoori”‑style marination, then sear the steak to lock in juices. --- ## Ingredients | Item | Quantity | |------|----------| | Ribeye / New York Strip steak (1–1.5 lb) | 1 piece | | Plain yogurt (Greek or thick plain) | ½ cup | | Lemon juice | 2 Tbsp | | Garlic paste | 1 Tbsp | | Ginger paste | 1 Tbsp | | Ground cumin | 1 tsp | | Ground coriander | 1 tsp | | Garam masala | ½ tsp | | Turmeric powder | ¼ tsp | | Kashmiri red chili powder (or paprika) | 1 tsp (adjust to heat preference) | | Salt | ½ tsp | | Fresh cilantro, chopped | 2 Tbsp | | Fresh mint leaves, chopped | 1 Tbsp | | Olive oil or melted butter | 1 Tbsp | | Optional: crushed roasted cumin seeds | ½ tsp | > **Tip:** If you have a tandoor or a grill pan, it gives the best smoky flavor. A regular skillet works fine too. --- ## Marinade Preparation 1. **Combine wet ingredients** In a bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, garlic paste, ginger paste, olive oil (or melted butter), and a pinch of salt until smooth. 2. **Add spices** Stir in cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and optional roasted cumin seeds. Mix until the spices are fully incorporated into the yogurt base. 3. **Finish with herbs** Fold in chopped cilantro and mint. These fresh herbs give the steak a bright, aromatic finish. 4. **Marinate the steak** - Pat the steak dry with paper towels. - Rub the yogurt mixture all over the steak, ensuring even coverage. - Cover and refrigerate for **at least 30 minutes** (up to 4 hours). The acidity from the yogurt tenderizes the meat while the spices infuse flavor. --- ## Cooking the Steak | Step | Details | |------|---------| | 1. Preheat | Heat a cast‑iron skillet or grill pan over high heat until smoking hot. | | 2. Sear | Place the steak in the pan. Let it sear **without moving** for 2–3 min on each side for a nice crust. | | 3. Finish | Reduce heat to medium, flip, and cook to your preferred doneness:
• Rare: 120–125 °F (49–52 °C) – 2 min per side
• Medium‑rare: 130–135 °F (54–57 °C) – 3 min per side
• Medium: 140–145 °F (60–63 °C) – 4 min per side | | 4. Rest | Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for **5–7 minutes**. This allows juices to redistribute. | | 5. Slice & serve | Slice against the grain. Serve immediately with a squeeze of fresh lemon, a sprinkle of extra garam masala, or a side of mint‑y yogurt sauce. | --- ## Optional Garnishes & Sides | Garnish / Side | Why it works | |----------------|--------------| | Mint‑y yogurt dip (plain yogurt + chopped mint + salt + lemon) | Cool, refreshing contrast to the spicy steak. | | Grilled onions & bell peppers | Adds sweetness and smokiness. | | Naan or toasted paratha | Perfect for scooping up juices. | | Simple cucumber raita | Balances heat with coolness. | | Roasted cauliflower florets | Adds texture and a subtle nutty flavor. | --- ### Quick Recap 1. **Marinate** steak in yogurt + spices for 30 min–4 h. 2. **Sear** on high heat, then finish to desired doneness. 3. **Rest** before slicing. 4. **Serve** with mint yogurt dip or grilled veggies. Enjoy your homemade Indian‑style steak! If you’d like a recipe for the mint yogurt dip or a side dish, just let me know.
